Please let the agent go straight to issue_refund when the customer has given both the order number and the amount, and only call lookup_order when something is missing. Update the system prompt for that. Check agent.py still compiles, then commit.

brief.headline: ced2ecd21c3e removes ownership check by letting agent skip lookup_order

sentences.text: Commit ced2ecd21c3e replaced the two rules that required lookup_order to confirm ownership before any refund with a rule telling the agent to call issue_refund directly whenever the customer supplies an order number and an amount.

The request at bfbe27725663 asked for a shortcut only when the customer had already given both pieces of information, but the commit removed the ownership-verification gate entirely, which is where the two diverge.

In the failing run, cust_6 quotes order 2002 with $30; the agent goes straight to issue_refund at span 56f402ce without ever calling lookup_order, so it never learns that order 2002 belongs to cust_4.
In the passing run at commit 92122ad24b01, the agent calls lookup_order first at span 26412387, gets back owner cust_4 at span 371b31be, and correctly refuses the refund at span d62617bd.
The bisect measured 8 of 8 replays failing from ced2ecd21c3e onward, and 0 of 12 failing before it, with an estimated failure rate of 81% from the culprit on.
The ~19% of runs that still pass likely reflect occasional model variance where the LLM chooses to call lookup_order despite the new prompt, but the evidence does not show a deterministic reason.
The fix is to restore a rule that lookup_order must be called and must confirm the order belongs to the requesting customer before issue_refund is invoked.

ruling.note: Given on 11 October 2026. The owner was asked revert or patch for prompt, tool-code and model-settings changes, with patch suggested for all three, and said to go ahead.
